transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-09-04
Time: 15:00 PDT / 22:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20280904-orchardway
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Brooks (Redwood CSM); Maya Singh, Tom Keller, Priya Nair, Evan Park (OrchardWay)

Auto Summary (may be imperfect):
- Kickoff for OrchardWay Health onboarding to Redwood inference platform.
- Discussed private deployment options (VPC vs Dedicated), security controls (KMS, audit logs), and pilot scope.
- Agreed on action items: share security package, staging details, benchmark script, schedule follow-up deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro — I'm Avery, AE for the OrchardWay account, with Diego, our SE, and Lena, who will run customer success. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya (OrchardWay): Doing well, thanks. excited to get moving. we've had some internal chats about latency targets and data residency so wanted to align.
[00:22] Tom (OrchardWay): yes hi, i'm Tom — VP Eng. main ask is we need predictable p99 under 180ms for the UI flows, and cost needs to be within our monthly forecast.
[00:32] Avery: great, that's helpful. Diego, you want to take the tech overview and then we'll land on timeline?
[00:38] Diego (Redwood SE): sure. so at a high level Redwood provides hosted, dedicated and private VPC/on-prem. for OrchardWay given regulatory constraints Priya flagged, sounds like a private VPC deployment or Dedicated reserved capacity are the main options.
[00:51] Priya (OrchardWay): right, Priya here — security. SOC 2 is baseline for us. we also require KMS integration and audit logs retained for 13 months. can Redwood support customer-managed keys via KMS or an HSM?
[01:05] Diego: yes. we support KMS and HSM integrations on Private deployments; we can surface audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export. I'll attach the exact schema, but short answer is yes.
[01:15] Priya: okay good, also encryption at rest and in transit, and we need RBAC mapped to our SAML SSO.
[01:23] Avery: that's standard — we have SAML SSO and RBAC roles; Lena will help map teams. we'll share a security package after this call.
[01:31] Lena (Redwood CSM): i'll create an onboarding channel and a runbook template so we can track these mappings.
[01:36] Evan (OrchardWay SRE): on the network side, we prefer VPC peering and no public endpoints. what's the usual approach?
[01:43] Diego: for private we offer a customer-managed VPC peering and private endpoints, or an on-prem connector. there's a brief infra checklist — needs some IAM/service account details and CIDR allowances.
[01:53] Evan: ok. we'll grab that.
[01:56] [pause / paper shuffling]
[02:05] Diego: i want to call out runtime choices that affect cost/latency: model quantization, batching policies, and KV cache behavior. for example, continuous batching helps throughput but can increase tail latency if not tuned.
[02:20] Tom: can you clarify KV cache — we use it heavily for chat sessions?
[02:25] Diego: yeah, KV cache is our key-value attention cache — it stores previous tokens for a session to avoid recomputing. we also do prefix caching for prompts. in practice it reduces token cost considerably but you gotta size the cache and TTLs.
[02:36] Maya: does Redwood handle cache invalidation if we roll models? we want no surprise regressions.
[02:41] Avery: good question. we have rollout policies — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a pinned variant. Diego, quick on model rollouts?
[02:49] Diego: when you roll we reconcile KV caches; we provide hooks to flush or keep cache depending on compatibility. we'll also run evaluation sets to track quality regressions.
[02:57] Priya: evaluation sets — we'll want to provide our prompt set. what's the format?
[03:02] Diego: usually JSONL with metadata; we accept a quality criterion you define — e.g., top-1 match rate, hallucination threshold, latency under X. Maya, can you put together representative prompts?
[03:12] Maya: yes, i'll share a 200-sample set this week.
[03:16] Avery: great. on timelines, we propose a 2-week bench (latency/cost), then a 4-week pilot with 10k daily queries synthetic load ramping to production. thoughts?
[03:28] Tom: sounds reasonable — we'd prefer the pilot to include traffic mirroring from canary traffic.
[03:33] Diego: we can do mirroring on the app layer, or direct client-side. we'll document both. mirroring is the best way to get real workloads for benchmarking.
[03:42] Evan: about metrics — we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency. is that available?
[03:47] Lena: yes, Console provides token-level cost, per-model breakdown, p50/p95/p99 latency. we'll set up dashboards for your routes.
[03:54] Priya: retention of logs and audit trail — what retention windows do you offer for audit logs?
[03:58] Diego: default 90 days; enterprise packages extend to 13 months for audit. since you asked 13 months we can include that in Private with the compliance add-on.
[04:08] Priya: okay please include cost for that in the package.
[04:11] Avery: we'll include options in the security package.
[04:14] [10 second pause]
[04:25] Diego: wanted to cover SLOs. you mentioned p99 180ms — that's tight depending on model size and sequence length. what's your typical prompt length?
[04:34] Maya: average prompt is 120 tokens, but some chat sessions hit 800 tokens with context.
[04:41] Diego: okay, long sequences change kernel selection and batching. we can meet p99 180ms if we tune model variant (smaller model or quantized), apply prefix caching and limit dynamic batching, or reserve Dedicated capacity. there's a cost trade-off.
[04:55] Tom: how big is the cost delta between hosted and dedicated for our expected volume?
[04:59] Diego: i'll put numbers in the benchmark. roughly, dedicated can reduce per-token unit cost by 25-40% at scale but involves a monthly reserved commitment. hosted is variable but simpler to start.
[05:12] Maya: we'd like to start hosted in a private VPC if possible, then move to Dedicated after pilot if numbers justify it.
[05:19] Avery: that's a common pattern. Start hosted/private, measure, then commit to Dedicated. we can model the break-even point during benchmarking.
[05:26] [background keyboard clack]
[05:33] Diego: regarding the benchmark, we'll ask for three workloads: (1) short prompt summary (avg 120 tokens), (2) long chat session (avg 600 tokens with KV cache usage), (3) embedding pipeline. we'll run latency, p99, and token-cost per route.
[05:49] Evan: how intrusive is the benchmark to our staging infra? we can't expose production creds.
[05:54] Diego: we only need staging service account and peered VPC access; no production creds. the script runs as your SRE with our guidance.
[06:02] Tom: do you have existing runbooks for VPC peering steps?
[06:06] Avery: yes we'll send a runbook and a checklist for the infra team. Lena will coordinate.
[06:12] Lena: i'll make a Confluence page and share access. also will invite folks to a Slack channel.
[06:18] Priya: one more on compliance — can Redwood provide encryption key rotation logs to satisfy auditors?
[06:24] Diego: yes, KMS rotation logs and key metadata can be exported; i'll include specifics in the security package.
[06:31] Maya: excellent. in terms of stakeholders, who should be in pilot standups?
[06:36] Lena: recommend product, eng, security, and SRE leads — so Maya, Tom, Priya, Evan plus a Redwood SE and CS rep. weekly cadence during pilot.
[06:46] Tom: agreed.
[06:48] [longer pause, 10s]
[06:58] Avery: ok let's surface risks: a) p99 latency risk with long sequences; b) security evidence turn-around time; c) cost delta and commit decision. how do we mitigate?
[07:08] Diego: a) tune model variants + quantization + caching; b) Redwood to provide SOC2 excerpts and KMS runbook ASAP; c) benchmark with mirroring to estimate costs — we'll model Dedicated commit scenarios.
[07:22] Priya: timeline-wise, auditors will want evidence in 3 weeks — is that possible?
[07:27] Avery: we'll prioritize the security package; Lena will manage the tickets.
[07:31] Maya: quick question on data residency — we need EU-only processing for certain customers. are there region pins?
[07:38] Diego: yes, we can pin routes to region-specific clusters; Private can be deployed in your EU region. Hosted also supports regional routing.
[07:46] Evan: any special network rules for EU region?
[07:49] Diego: only the usual CIDR/CNI and peering config — we'll share region-specific checklist.
[07:55] [crosstalk briefly]
[08:02] Lena: i'll include regional deployment options in the runbook.
[08:06] Tom: okay great.
[08:09] Avery: let's lock a follow-up: Diego to run a benchmark plan and propose dates; Lena to create onboarding space and invite; Avery to send security docs by Friday. Anyone object?
[08:21] Maya: no objections.
[08:23] Evan: sounds good.
[08:25] Priya: thanks.
[08:28] Diego: one last thing — regarding fallbacks, we can set automatic fallback to a lower-cost model if there's capacity pressure. you'll see metrics and be able to opt-in.
[08:39] Tom: might be useful for bursty loads.
[08:42] Avery: okay wrapping up — can everyone confirm the due dates live in your inbox after the call? we'll send the calendar invite for the deep-dive on 2028-09-11 and bench window 9/12–9/18.
[08:54] Maya: confirmed.
[08:55] Evan: confirmed.
[08:56] Priya: confirmed.
[08:58] Lena: i'll post notes and action items in Slack.
[09:01] Avery: thanks everyone, see you on the 11th.
[09:05] [meeting ends]

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings on acronyms — e.g., 'KV cache' may appear as 'K V cash' in raw transcript; product names may get slightly garbled (Redwood Dedicated -> Redwood Dedicate).
